answer: Sustained Attention Ledger.** Each identity must hold a live session with a registered endpoint that logs continuous sub-second task responses; idle gaps void the entry. To open an identity, an attacker deposits copper credits into a shared vault, forfeited if the session lapses below a rolling threshold. Because parallel sybils fragment one operator's attention, each fake identity demands its own sustained response budget, multiplying labor and latency costs without bound. A grove of identities thus costs linearly more attention than it can spoof.
